skill.description: Validate deployment and application configuration with schemas, environment rules, tests, migrations, secure handling, and generated documentation.

security_audit.summary: The audit confirms one high-risk static finding: broad discovery includes `.env*` files and reads matched configuration content. Most code-fence and template-literal detections are false positives. A separate semantic issue remains because runtime change events emit complete configuration objects that may contain sensitive values.

remediation.issue: Environment files may be scanned and read during configuration discovery.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before reading `.env*` files, restrict scans to approved project roots, and redact secret values in all output.

remediation.issue: Runtime change events may include complete old and new configuration objects.
remediation.suggestion: Redact sensitive keys before emitting, logging, or comparing configuration changes in generated implementations.

remediation.issue: Example scan patterns do not define default ignore rules.
remediation.suggestion: Add ignore rules for dependency folders, build outputs, VCS directories, and files outside the requested project scope.

content.value_statement: Configuration mistakes can break deployments and expose secrets. This skill helps validate schemas, environment rules, tests, migrations, and documentation before release.
actual_capabilities: Identifies configuration files across JSON, YAML, TOML, INI, env, and config.js patterns.
Guides JSON Schema validation with AJV custom formats.
Defines environment-specific rules for development, staging, and production.
Outlines Jest tests for valid and invalid configuration values.
Provides examples for migrations, encryption, and generated reference documentation.
limitations: Provides implementation patterns, not a packaged validator.
Example snippets need project-specific functions and imports before use.
Does not verify live infrastructure or deployment platforms by itself.
Secret scanning examples require approval, masking, and scope controls.

use_cases.title: Pre-Release Config Review
use_cases.description: Review configuration files before release and find missing fields, unsafe defaults, and environment drift.

use_cases.title: Schema-Driven Validation
use_cases.description: Create validation schemas, custom formats, and tests for service settings used across environments.

use_cases.title: Configuration Security Checks
use_cases.description: Flag weak production settings, possible secret exposure, HTTP endpoints, and missing encryption requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my application configuration files. Identify required fields, environment differences, unsafe defaults, and clear validation gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Create Validation Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Create JSON Schema validation rules for my service configuration. Include URL, port, duration, and production-only requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Build Config Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a configuration test suite for CI. Cover valid examples, invalid values, environment rules, and security failures.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Runtime Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a runtime configuration validation and migration strategy. Include reload behavior, version handling, redaction, and failure policies.

output_examples.input: Review staging and production configuration before release.
output: A configuration analysis listing file types, environment coverage, and missing required settings.
A validation plan with schema rules, production checks, and tests.
A security section that flags possible secret exposure and weak deployment defaults.

output_examples.input: Create validation rules for a database service configuration.
output: A schema design with hostname, port, database, user, password, and SSL requirements.
Custom validation rules for safe ports and required production encryption.
Test cases for accepted settings and rejected invalid values.

output_examples.input: Prepare runtime validation for configuration changes.
output: A reload plan that validates new configuration before applying changes.
Failure handling rules for development and production environments.
Redaction guidance for events, logs, and security reports.

best_practices: Require explicit approval before reading files that may contain secrets.
Validate production settings more strictly than development settings.
Keep schemas, tests, migrations, and documentation synchronized.
anti_patterns: Do not print raw secrets in validation errors or reports.
Do not reuse development defaults in production without review.
Do not scan broad directories without ignore rules and user scope.

faq.question: Does this skill run a validator by itself?
faq.answer: No. It guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to design validation logic and review configuration safely.

faq.question: Can it help with JSON Schema?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes patterns for schema validation, custom formats, and structured validation errors.

faq.question: Does it support environment-specific rules?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers development, staging, and production rules such as debug mode, HTTPS, and encryption.

faq.question: Can it detect secrets in configuration files?
faq.answer: It can guide secret checks, but sensitive files need explicit approval and redacted output.

faq.question: Will the example snippets work unchanged?
faq.answer: No. Some snippets are templates and need project-specific imports, helper functions, and tests.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: DevOps engineers, backend developers, and security reviewers who manage deployment configuration can use it.
